summary: 1924 steel fire tower on Guyandotte (Bolt) Mountain, WV, administered by the WV Division of Forestry; NHLR-registered 2015; poor condition after a fire per 2016 report.

facts.design: steel tower with four legs and a glass-enclosed observation cab; about 65 feet high in a 1952 station description
facts.status_note: Standing per register and association list; a 2016 visit report rates it in poor condition after a fire damaged stairs and cab glass

staffing.status: observer on duty in 1960 per newspaper; no later staffing record found

visit.trail_note: Access road leads from WV 99 to the site, per NHLR; the 2016 visit report rates the tower in poor condition

events.note: Earlier tower at this site, described as the first fire tower in West Virginia
Present tower built by Emory Wriston to replace the 1916 tower
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: steel, four legs, about 65 feet high, glass-enclosed cab, land leased by U.S. Forest Service
Concrete block cabin, 20 by 22 feet, built to replace a small frame shed used for living quarters
State conservation employee assisted at the tower in August 1960 while the regular observer was in the hospital
November 1, 2016 visit report: poor condition; fire had damaged stairs and blown out cab glass (fire date not given)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says Raleigh County; Forest Lookouts header says Raleigh/Wyoming Counties; the association list and the 1952 station description say Wyoming. The story reports the disagreement and keeps the register's Raleigh County in the record.

notes_for_editor: No height in the brief; the 1952 'about 65 feet' figure may describe a later structure than the 1924 tower and is kept in design text, not height_m. The 1924 build and the 1916 predecessor rest on the register alone. The fire's date is not given in any source I could read. Current public access and ownership of the site are unknown. The 1987 Goldenseal article and the Wriston PDF linked from the register were not readable (the PDF returned no text). Reddit and POI Factory pages were not used as sources.
